findings.where: "Where we're starting" section: the Canggu, Uluwatu and Kuta Lombok destination cards with their "Best hostels ›" lines (parts p8–p10), reached from the hero's "Explore destinations" button and the nav's "Destinations" link
findings.fault: Every route to the destination guides ends at three cards that cannot be clicked, even though each looks like a link with its arrow, hover rule and boxed card. Sending visitors on to the guides is one of the page's three jobs, and the second call to action ends at a dead end.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker on a phone who taps "Explore destinations" and then "Best hostels" for Canggu and gets nothing back. The only working content on the site is hidden from them, and a pre-launch brand loses credibility at its first broken tap.

findings.where: "How we rank" in the nav and in the footer (parts p4, p14)
findings.fault: The page's one way of backing its central claim, that it ranks hostels "on merit alone", links back to this same page. The ranking method is promised but never shown.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who has learned to distrust ranking sites and clicks to see what "merit" means finds nothing. The product treats a published method as its basis for trust, so an empty link makes the claim look like marketing.

findings.where: Footer: Privacy, Terms and Report content (parts p12, p13, p15)
findings.fault: The legal and reporting links look real but all point back to this page, so the page asks for contact details while its privacy terms cannot be read.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deciding whether to hand over their email address checks Privacy and finds nothing. A hostel owner reached by cold outreach, checking whether this is a real business, sees the same empty links.

findings.where: Hero: the coral "Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news" button (part p6)
findings.fault: Signing up means opening a mail app and writing an email. The button gives no wording to send and doesn't say what launch news will contain, when it will come, or that the visitor can stop it. There is no risk-reversal line at the main action.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker mid-trip on a phone, often on a poor connection or with no mail app set up, who would have given an address in one tap but won't write an email to a stranger without knowing what they're signing up for.

findings.where: Hero: the line above the heading, "The better way to find hostels in Indonesia.", and the heading itself, which is only the wordmark "MantaHostels"
findings.fault: The loudest promise is a vague comparison (better than what?), and the heading names the brand without making a promise. The specific claims (merit-only ranking, booking direct or through your usual site) sit in small body text, so the 5-second test turns up a slogan rather than a reason to care.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker scanning for a reason to use another hostel site besides the ones they already know. The rules file asks for the loud half to be a claim with plain, specific mechanics beneath it, and an unsupported "better" is the kind of line that makes them skeptical.

findings.where: Whole page: hero, destination section and footer
findings.fault: Nothing on the page says who is behind it apart from "luc" in an email address. There is no name, no line about the founder and no proof of any kind. The product has no proof yet, so the person building it is the only credibility on offer, and the page doesn't use it.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor or a cold-contacted hostel owner deciding whether to trust an unknown pre-launch site with their email or their business. With no reviews or partners yet, a named and reachable founder is what they would look for.

findings.where: Footer line "Launching across Indonesia · piloting now in Bali" next to the "Where we're starting" cards, which include Kuta Lombok
findings.fault: The footer says the pilot is in Bali only, while the section above lists a Lombok destination as a starting point. Neither gives a launch timeframe, so the visitor cannot tell what exists now.
findings.who_objects: A traveller heading to Lombok who wants to know if the guide covers them now or later, and who reads the mismatch as carelessness.
